full_judgment:
Land measuring 18.41 decimals out of 147 decimals appertaining to CS and SA plot No.3068 under CS Khatian No.1141 and SA khatian No.1093 corresponding to RS plot No.5700 under RS khatian No.291 and mutation khatian No.3676 of mouja Duptera, JL No.156, Police Station-Araihazar, District-Dhaka at present Narayanganj is the suit land. The land measuring 147 decimals of CS plot No.3068 under CS khatian No.1141 was rightly recorded in the name of Bohor Ali Munshi and Bashir Uddin. In an amicable settlement with his brother Bohor Ali Munshi, Bashir Uddin Munshi got said [47 decimals of land. Bashir Uddin Munshi died, leaving 3(three) sons, namely Khaleque Bhuiyan, Alek Bhuiyan, and Almas Bhuiyan, and 2(two) daughters, namely Jamina and Ayesha. Subsequently, Khaleque Bhuiyan died, leaving a wife, Lutfun Nessa. By registered partition deed No.2164 dated 27-6-1972, Alek Bhuiyan got 48 decimals of land, and Almas Bhuiyan got 96 decimals. Almas Bhuiyan died leaving behind 4(four) sons, namely AKM Sanaul Hogue Bhuiyan, Sirajullah Bhuiyan, Muhammed Ali Bhuiyan, Nisiruddin, and 3(three) daughters, namely Parul Akter, Bulbul Akter, and Parveen Akhter and a wife, Shamsun Nahar. Among the legal heirs of the late Almas Bhuiyan, partition deed No, 4075 dated 31-12-1979 was executed. According to said partition deed Shamsun Nahar, the wife of late Almas Bhuiyan, and his 2(two) minor sons and daughter, Nasiruddin and Parveen Akhter, got 53 decimals of land. Then, Shamsun Nahar, Nasiruddin, and Parveen Akhter sold 53 decimals of land, including the suit land, to the plaintiff and his other brothers by registered deed Nos. 5492, 26626 and 26627, all dated 25-7-1980 and 15637 dated 28-7-1980 (Exhibits 6-9). Nasiruddin Bhuiyan and Parveen Akhter again sold 36 decimals of land out of said 53 decimals to the plaintiff by registered deed No.3194 dated 16-6-1986 (Exhibit 12) pursuant to a deed of agreement for sale date 9-1-1986. 

 13. Mr Md Ibrahim Mollah, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party, on the other hand, submits that both the courts below, having found prima facie title and possession over the suit land in favour of the plaintiff rightly decreed the suit and, as such, concurrent finding of the courts below need not be interfered with by this Court sitting on revisional jurisdiction. The learned Advocate submits further that failure to prove title by the plaintiff in a suit for permanent injunction cannot disentitle him to a decree for a permanent injunction if he can prove possession over the suit land and since the plaintiff having produced oral and documentary evidence such as mutation khatian, rent receipts avail to prove the prima facie title and possession over the suit land he got the decree for a permanent injunction. The learned Advocate again submits that the finding of facts arrived at by the courts below are immune from the interference of this Court sitting on a revisional jurisdiction if those findings are not perverse and as no perversity is found with the findings of the courts below, the Rule should be discharged. The learned Advocate submits further that in a suit for permanent injunction, if the plaintiff can prove his exclusive possession over the suit land, he is entitled to get the decree and the instant case, both the courts below found exclusive possession of the plaintiff over the suit land and, as such, nothing remains to interfere into such concurrent findings of the courts below. To substantiate his submission, the learned Advocate in this regard refers to reliance in the cases of 1) 3 ADC 124, 2) 1995 BLD 509, and 3) 1984 BLD (AD) 285. 

 20. Moreover, failure to prove title by the plaintiff in a suit for permanent injunction cannot disentitle him to a decree for a permanent injunction if he can prove possession only. The rent receipts are evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title. In the instant case, the plaintiff having produced mutation khatian No.3676, rent receipts, and having examined oral evidence, could prove his prima facie possession and title over the suit land. So, both the courts below, concurrently having found prima .facie title and possession over the suit land in favour of the plaintiff, decreed the suit.
